title: Scrap Pirates Region Response V5
description: Defines durable regional world content for AI generation. Omit collections and optional fields when there is nothing meaningful to say; mission-specific characters, cargo, and transient story state belong in mission responses.

factions.description: Factions introduced by this region. Omit when the region introduces none.

systems.description: Star systems defined by this response.

locations.description: Dockable stations or landable ports. All inhabited systems should have at least one.

equipmentDefinitions.description: Custom equipment definitions introduced by this region. Omit when there are none.

shipCards.description: Custom ship type definitions introduced by this region. Omit when there are none.

decks.description: Weighted content decks introduced by this region. Omit when there are none.

FactionRelation.description: Non-neutral starting relationship from one faction to another. Omit neutral relationships.

factionRef.description: Name of the faction or allegiance this relationship points to.

stance.description: Starting stance toward the referenced faction.

Faction.description: A durable faction the DM can use for ownership, conflict, encounters, and world reactions.

name.description: Player-facing faction name; also used by factionRef fields.

affinity.description: Gameplay affinity/color. Blue often fits corporate factions, Yellow often fits sparrows, and Green often fits authoritarians or brigands. Red is for rare advanced, secretive, or alien factions.

description.description: What the faction wants, how it behaves, and what makes interacting with it distinctive.

shipDecks.description: Custom ship deck IDs, up to one per color. Omitted classes use the default/fallback deck. This can be left blank for most small factions, as they lack the resources to make custom ships.

moduleDecks.description: Custom ship deck IDs, up to one per color. Omitted classes use the default/fallback deck. This can be left blank for most small factions, as they lack the resources to make custom ships.

relations.description: Explicit non-neutral relationships to other factions. Unlisted factions are Neutral. The values in the allegiance enum are also valid relations targets.

secretInfo.description: Hidden motives, internal politics, leverage, or truths available to the AI DM but not revealed by default.

hostileToPlayer.description: Initial hostility toward the captain. Default false.

friendlyToPlayer.description: Initially friendly to the captain; automatic support when joining a fight against a non-friendly side. Hostility overrides friendship. Default false.

stature.description: Narrative scale or role of the faction.

allegiance.description: Galaxy-wide groups that the faction fits into for determining hostility. If another faction is hostie to this faction's allegiance, it is also hostile to this faction. A faction can be hostile to its own allegiance - for example, a particular brigand outfit might be hostile to other brigands.

System.description: Canonical facts for one generated star system.

address.description: Coordinate identity: 1–13 digits, each 1–7. The galaxy uses a tree structure, where parent systems remove a digit and child systems add a digit, and parents and children can be traversed.

controllerRef.description: Stable faction ID of the primary governing faction. If blank, falls back to the Syndicate.

minorRef.description: Stable faction ID of a secondary faction that visits this system. If the system is a conflict zone, this is the other faction in the conflict. Falls back to Brigands.

description.description: Concise canonical identity of the system: what would the local traders know about it?

civilianRef.description: Civilian faction associated with the system, or null when none is defined.

Location.description: A dockable station or landable planetary port inside a system.

description.description: What this place is, what happens here, and why a player might care about it.

services.description: Recognized services the player can access here. Omit when none are available. Common: Repair, Job Board, Trade. Uncommon: Outfitter. Rare: Shipyard, Junkyard.

appearance.description: Short visual brief for depicting the location.

secretInfo.description: Information about this location that's initially hidden from the player, but used by the DM. Internal politics, underworld dealings, secret bases - that kind of thing.

techLevel.description: How technologically advanced is this location? Affects ship spawning in orbit, and sold goods quality. 0 is uninhabited or technologically regressed. 1-4 is a spacer-town, 5-10 is more of a bustling city. A major center of a regional power might be 11-20, while core worlds are 20+

hidden.description: Initially omitted from player navigation until RevealLocation in a mission.

shots.description: Shots produced by one activation. Usually 1-4; higher damage generally means fewer shots. Yellow cannons tend to use more shots and smaller dieSides.

baseDiceCount.description: Attack dice rolled per shot. Usually 1; very powerful cannons may use 2-3.

dieSides.description: Faces on each base attack die. Typical dice are d4, d6, d8, d10, d12, or d20. Balance die size against shots, dice count, and effects.

EquipmentDefinition.description: Immutable equipment definition available to ships or markets.

id.description: Stable ID used by deck entries and other references.

category.description: Determines where the equipment might show up, and the price. For example, economy modules are used for merchants, not warships.

defense.description: Defense used by combat targeting/resolution. Delicate civilian equipment is often 1-3, cannons 3-5, and armor 5-7. Red modules might be 6-13 depending on their category.

inputs.description: Exactly three slots that must be connected by the player, top/middle/bottom. Colors must be distinct. With two inputs use [color, "", otherColor]. At least one input is required or the client will discard this equipment.  More powerful equipment can be balanced by needing more slots.

weapon.description: Weapon profile when this equipment is a weapon. Omit for non-weapons.

effects.description: Registered engine effects applied by this equipment. Omit when it has no special effects. Most non-red equipment has zero or one effect type, but some effect types are designed to be specified in multiple EquipmentEffect objects.

basePrice.description: Base market price before local modifiers.

description.description: Player facing description that explains the item.

ShipCard.description: There are default ship cards as fallbacks for civilian use, but some factions are powerful or wealthy enough to have custom ship cards.

id.description: Stable ID used by ship decks.

class.description: Ship class, typically small, medium, large, or capital.

portraitBrief.description: Visual brief for the ship portrait.

coreDefense.description: Base defense of the ship core. Generally 2-4 for small or civilian ships, 3-5 for medium ships, and 6-10 for large ships.

warship.description: If true, this ship will not use economy modules - only cannons and defense modules.

lootFuel.description: A list of fuel tokens recoverable from a destroyed instance of this ship. Duplicate fuel tokens are expected - a ship might drop 4-12 depending on size and cargo capacity, and weighted towards the affinity color.

lootHull.description: A list of hull cards recoverable from a destroyed instance of this ship. Duplicate entries are expected.  A ship might drop 1-5 depending on size, and weighted towards the affinity color.

shipSystems.description: A list of functional ship system slots. Ship instances will draw from the faction's moduleDecks of the appropriate color for each slot, or the fallback civilian modules. Duplicate entries are expected. A ship would have roughly 2/4/6/10 for small/medium/large/capital class, with (rare) red systems being twice as strong as the others.

DeckEntry.description: Weighted entry in a generated content deck.

definitionRef.description: ID of the equipment definition or ship card drawn by this entry. Add a blank one to allow default/civilian ships in the deck, and use deck IDs to incorporate other decks.

weight.description: Relative positive draw weight (number of copies in the deck.)

Deck.description: Weighted content deck referenced by factions or encounters.

id.description: Stable deck ID used by faction deck bindings.

kind.description: Definition category drawn by this deck - Ship or Module. Don't mix both Ships and Modules in one deck.

class.description: Ship class restriction for a class-specific deck. Omit when not class-specific.

entries.description: The actual contents of this deck.
